questions.question: Electricity: first 350 kWh at R2,00, above that R2,50. A household using 420 kWh pays, before VAT:
The final step on most tariff bills, applied to the R875,00 subtotal:
R5 000 at 6% for three years: simple interest gives R5 900,00, compound gives:
A R120,00 item rising with 5% inflation for two years costs:
options: R132,00 — add 5% of the original twice
R132,30 — 120 × 1,05², each rise works on the new price

subtopics.title: VAT, Income Tax and Exchange Rates

questions.question: A till slip total of R287,50 INCLUDES VAT. The price excluding VAT is:
options: 287,50 ÷ 1,15 = R250,00 — division unwinds the 15% charged on the smaller amount

questions.question: On a payslip, net pay is:
options: Gross salary minus deductions — what actually reaches the bank

questions.question: Taxable income R310 000; bracket: R42 678 + 26% of the amount above R237 100; rebate R17 235. Annual tax:
At R18,50 per US dollar with a 2% fee, a $120 purchase costs:

subtopics.title: Summarising Data: Mean, Median and Quartiles

questions.question: For the arranged marks 34, 41, 45, 52, 55, 58, 61, 66, 72, 78, 85, the median is:
options: 58 — the sixth of eleven arranged values

questions.question: The mean of the same eleven marks, with sum 647:
options: 58,8 — 647 ÷ 11, the balancing point of the data

questions.question: Q1 = 45 and Q3 = 72 for that data set. The interquartile range is:
options: 27 — Q3 minus Q1, the width of the middle half, immune to extremes

questions.question: For data containing an extreme outlier, the honest average is usually:
options: The mean, because it uses every value
The median — outliers drag the mean but barely move the middle position

subtopics.title: Representing Data and Spotting Misleading Graphs

questions.question: The five-number summary — minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum — is drawn as a:
Two classes share a median of 58, but Class A's box plot is much narrower. The full comparison sentence is:
options: Class A is better at everything
Equally strong at the centre, but Class A is more consistent — same median, smaller interquartile range
Class B has a higher median

questions.question: A bar graph's money axis starts at 45 instead of 0. The effect is:
options: A rise from 50 to 55 looks like a doubling, because the bars show only their tips

questions.question: A survey about taxi fares conducted only among car owners is flawed because:
options: The sample is biased — it cannot speak for the commuters the question is about

questions.question: Chips bought at R6,50, sold at R10,00. The percentage mark-up is:
An invoice reads R250,00 EXCLUDING VAT. The amount that leaves the account is:
options: R250,00 — excluding means no VAT applies
R287,50 — VAT of R37,50 still gets added

questions.question: Why is taking 15% OF an inclusive total and subtracting it wrong?
options: Because subtraction is never allowed in finance
Because the 15% was charged on the smaller, exclusive price — only dividing by 1,15 unwinds it

questions.question: R200,00 paid monthly into a stokvel for a year accumulates:
options: R2 400,00 — saved, but not grown; a stokvel returns what members put in

questions.question: R5 000,00 at 6% COMPOUND for two years grows to:
options: R5 618,00 — R5 300,00 after year one, then 5 300 × 1,06

questions.question: The R18,00 gap between compound and simple interest after two years is:
options: Year two's interest earned on year one's interest — and the gap widens every added year

questions.question: With 5% annual inflation, money kept in a tin at home:
options: Loses buying power — the R120,00 basket item costs R132,30 in two years while the tin stands still

questions.question: For the marks 62, 58, 71, 65 and 24: mean and median are:
Removing the flu-week 24 lifts the mean from 56,0 to 64,0. This shows:
options: One outlier dragged the mean down eight points while the median never flinched
Means should always exclude low marks

questions.question: The full Level 4 answer about which average is honest here:
options: Say the mean, with no reason
Name the median, name the 24 as an outlier, and say which way it pulls the mean

questions.question: The thumb test on the phone-shop poster works by:
options: Measuring the bars with a ruler
Covering the axis numbers — if the axis starts at R45 000 instead of zero, a small rise poses as a boom
